findings.message: Downstream TDD impact not separately enumerated. §3/§6/§9 enumerate SPEC inheritance well; the TDD layer is only seeded implicitly via §8 verification table and BDD cross-references. The specific TDD obligations (durability-at-ack crash probe, unique-constraint property test, fail-closed deny-on-grant-unavailable test, synchronous_commit config-drift assertion) are not explicitly named.
findings.recommendation: Add one line in §9 (Downstream) naming the TDD obligations this ADR seeds so the Test Architect inherits an explicit test surface rather than inferring it from §8.

findings.message: Sibling cross-references use BRD-topic refs as proxies for not-yet-authored ADR IDs (carried from iteration 1; acceptable). When sibling ADRs are authored the BRD proxy references must be replaced with @adr:/@depends: references, and no mechanical obligation pins that replacement to a specific cross-ADR ID.
findings.recommendation: When sibling ADRs land, replace each BRD proxy in §10 with the concrete @depends:/@adr: reference, keeping BRD origin as secondary anchor. No change required at this iteration.

findings.message: Re-scoped §8 p95 criterion resolves the prior P2 implementability concern. Residual: the 'no-cache MVP load envelope' budget the PK read must hit is not given a number at ADR altitude; acceptable, but worth a pointer so downstream SPEC/TDD authors know the envelope target is theirs to fix.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add a parenthetical in the §8 row noting the no-cache PK-read budget value is set at SPEC/TDD (downstream), distinct from the cache-gated p95 < 50 ms jointly owned with BRD.01.08.66e2. No P1/P2 remains.

findings.message: Halt-clear / resume transition undecided — standby-flap write-availability oscillation unbounded. §3 decides the primary halts create-path writes on synchronous-standby loss (fail-closed, RPO=0 preserved), but names only the entry into the halted state, never the exit. Auto-resume vs operator-gated resume is undecided, and there is no guard against standby flapping driving repeated halt/resume churn that can present as a retry-storm. §7 instruments standby loss (<=30s alert) but no signal or time bound governs recovery detection or debounced resume.
findings.recommendation: Decide the resume semantics in §3: auto-resume on confirmed standby re-sync vs operator-gated resume. If auto, add a debounce/hysteresis bound (e.g. require N seconds of healthy replica-lag-0 before re-opening writes). Add a §7 'standby recovered / writes resumed' signal with a time bound mirroring the existing <=30s loss alert.

findings.message: Create-path halt duration is unbounded — sustained single-standby outage is a distinct availability mode not related to RTO. RTO <= 30 min (§2) is defined for store loss via standby promotion, a different failure than a sustained single-standby outage where the primary survives but shorten stays halted. The create-path outage envelope on that branch has no stated bound and no relationship drawn to the 99.9% availability target.
findings.recommendation: State the recovery escalation for a sustained standby outage: how long the create-path halt is tolerated before an action (re-provision standby, or promote/reseed) is triggered. Relate it to the availability budget. Even 'halt tolerated up to T, then escalate to <action>' closes the gap.

findings.message: Planned standby maintenance trips the create-path halt — routine ops becomes a shorten outage under the MVP single-standby topology. Any planned standby operation (patching, restart, version upgrade) trips the same fail-closed halt as an unplanned loss. The ADR does not acknowledge this. With a single standby there is no maintenance path that keeps writes available.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge in §7 that planned standby maintenance trips the create-path halt under the MVP single-standby topology, and state the operational handling (maintenance window with shorten degraded-mode advertised, or note that 'Next cycle' read-replica/standby fan-out provides a maintenance-without-halt path).

findings.message: Rollback export asserts at-rest 'encrypted' control that §5 explicitly defers. §5 records at-rest encryption and key-management as deferred to the data-protection ADR (BRD.01.08.daeb). §7 rollback step (2) states the PII-column export 'inherits the access/at-rest controls (encrypted, least-privilege, secure-deleted)'. The word 'encrypted' asserts an at-rest export control whose algorithm/key-management has not been decided here. Not an uncovered control, but the export of a may-contain-PII column is precisely the moment the deferred at-rest control becomes load-bearing.
findings.recommendation: Make the export's at-rest dependency explicit: state that the rollback export of the PII column is gated on the data-protection ADR (BRD.01.08.daeb) at-rest controls being in place, or that the interim managed-tier volume encryption is the operative at-rest control for the export until then. Keeps §7 and §5 consistent on what 'encrypted' means pre-sibling-ADR.

findings.location: §7 Implementation Assessment — Monitoring baseline / MVP phases Phase 1
findings.message: synchronous_commit config-knob declaration still incomplete after fixer pass. The fixer added a monitoring hook ('Config drift — alert if synchronous_commit deviates') which surfaces the parameter name but does not supply the expected value (e.g., 'on'), the default value, or the configuration location (e.g., postgresql.conf or managed-service parameter group path). An operator cannot confirm the parameter is set correctly post-provisioning without consulting external documentation.
findings.recommendation: Expand the monitoring baseline entry for synchronous_commit to a full C5 config-knob declaration: parameter name (synchronous_commit), expected value (on), default (off in many managed tiers — note the divergence), and configuration location (postgresql.conf or managed-service parameter group). This lets an operator verify correctness at provisioning time and anchors the config-drift alert to a named expected value.
